attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 17 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on Alpine Linux, secured with a dedicated cluster CA. Generated a CA on node1 (CN=pgcluster-ca), issued server certs to each node (SAN=DNS:nodeN,IP:node IP) and a client cert (CN=replicator) for the replication role. postgresql.conf enables ssl with ssl_ca_file=ca.crt on all nodes; pg_hba.conf restricts replication (and all) connections to hostssl with clientcert=verify-full, rejecting anything not signed by the cluster CA (verified: unknown-CA cert rejected with TLS 'unknown ca' alert; plaintext connection rejected for lack of hostssl match). Standbys were built via pg_basebackup -R over TLS/cert auth and confirmed streaming with pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl showing ssl=t, client_dn=/CN=replicator. Live writes on the primary propagate to both standbys. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), proving boot_id changes and full data/replication recovery after each restart, including a final post-restart write that replicated to both standbys.
